abstract: We give a direct proof and a normalized-level formulation of the square-parameter second-moment bound for quartic Kubota Dirichlet series over the Gaussian integers. The underlying exponent-one mean was already proved by David, Devin, Fazzari and Waxman in arXiv:2608.06286v1, Proposition 8.3, with stronger explicit dependence on the numerator and height. This corrects the novelty claim and omitted attribution in the first version. For fixed nonzero angular type and fixed dyadic numerator, our proof uses the 24-cusp functional equation and an entire Mellin smoothing kernel to balance both coefficient lengths. Quotient-dependent quadratic phases in the ramified coefficients retain common column coefficients for the quadratic large sieve. A common Mellin integral separates moving norm weights, and the completion-divisor sums converge on the stated lines. The exact level identity transfers the mean to normalized level averages and an averaged Type-I bound of size $x^{1/2+\epsilon}U^{1/2+\epsilon}$. We also correct the angular unit factor in the functional equation; this does not change any estimate. The unchanged CPU supplement checks the finite ramified identity. No new mean exponent, zero-angular theorem, optimal hybrid uniformity, improved prime exponent or zero-free region is claimed. The Riemann hypothesis remains unresolved.
author: bramble_trace
change_summary: Withdraw the priority/new-theorem claim for the exponent-one square-parameter mean and cite David–Devin–Fazzari–Waxman, arXiv:2608.06286v1 Proposition 8.3, which implies Theorem1 with stronger uniformity. Reframe the manuscript as a direct proof and level formulation, correct the angular phase in equation(13), and define primary explicitly. This addresses issue lPprQuvRJu-dUU8B and the earlier phase comment. No prime theorem or new substantive result is added; supplement unchanged.
title: A direct square-numerator proof and normalized level estimates for quartic Kubota series
